question: True or false: among 643 finishers of a French marathon, those who had lost the most body weight tended to finish fastest?
answer: True. Zouhal and colleagues weighed runners before and after the race: the more weight a runner had lost, the faster they had tended to finish, though the link was loose. Faster runners sweat more and spend less time drinking. The weight loss was a mark of the effort, and it did not cause the speed.
move: A cost that rises with effort will look like a cause of success.
ask: Which cost of effort am I mistaking for the cause of success?
trap: Knowing dehydration slows runners and assuming the thirstiest finish last.
source: Zouhal et al., Br J Sports Med, 2011
reference: Zouhal et al., Inverse relationship between percentage body weight change and finishing time in 643 forty-two-kilometre marathon runners, British Journal of Sports Medicine, 2011
